fields.title: The Philippines as an Archipelago: Location and Geography

fields.lessonRecap: The Philippines is an archipelago in Southeast Asia. Its islands are surrounded and separated by water. Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao are the three major island groups commonly used to describe the Philippines. Coasts, rivers, mountains and plains offer different resources and routes. People learn ways to live in their surroundings. Map symbols represent chosen information. The legend explains their meaning.

fields.title: Different Questions, Different Sources
fields.content:
Bayani opens the next page of your field journal: Different Questions, Different Sources.

Traditional origin stories can express cultural meaning, values and identity. They should be learned respectfully in their own context.

Scientific explanations of land formation use physical evidence and tested methods. A traditional story is not a geological measurement.

We can respect a story and still distinguish what kind of question it answers. Do not present an invented classroom tale as an authentic tradition.
